This covers 11 digits that do not start with 1 (such as '2 555 123 4567'), fewer than 10 digits, 12 or more digits, and an international number like '+44 20 7946 0958'.

fmt_phone: Whenever letters or other words are mixed in with exactly 10 digits (such as 'CALL-555-123-4567'), the non-digit characters are thrown away and the number is formatted; but a vanity number with letters instead of digits ('1-800-FLOWERS') has too few digits and returns an empty string, not the original text. The same holds for any text that has at least one digit but fewer than 10, such as a seven-digit number with no area code ('555-0132'): it returns an empty string, not the text as typed.

fmt_phone: Whenever the area code or exchange begins with 0 or 1 (such as '0551234567' or '0155550132'), the number is still accepted and formatted in the usual way, exactly like any other 10-digit number: '0551234567' gives '(055) 123-4567' and '0155550132' gives '(015) 555-0132'. This also holds when the text is already written as (AAA) BBB-CCCC, such as '(015) 555-0132', which comes back as '(015) 555-0132' because it is formatted, not because it was passed through untouched. No check is made that the number is a valid North American number, and no such number is rejected or returned unformatted for having a 0 or 1 in those places. Only a single leading 1 on an 11-digit number is removed.
fmt_phone: Whenever the input is NULL, it returns NULL; whenever it is empty text, it returns empty text; whenever it has no digits ('abc'), it returns the text unchanged.

fmt_phone: Whenever the input is a plain number rather than text (such as 5551234567 or 15551234567), it is treated as its digits and formatted; a decimal number such as 5551234567.0 is not a valid North American number, because the extra digit makes 11 digits not starting with 1. It returns an empty string, not the text as typed.
fmt_phone: Whenever the digits are written in non-Western numerals (such as Arabic-Indic digits), they are not recognised as digits and the text is returned unchanged.

grade_letter: Whenever the score is 92 or more and no more than 100 it returns 'A'; 83 or more but under 92 returns 'B'; 71 or more but under 83 returns 'C'; 60 or more but under 71 returns 'D'; anything lower but not below 0 (0 or more but under 60) returns 'F'. A score above 100, extra credit included, is never an 'A' because it is invalid and returns 'X' (see rule 21). A score below 0 (such as -5 or -0.01) is never an 'F' because it is invalid and also returns 'X' (see rule 21).

grade_letter: Whenever the score is exactly on a boundary (92, 83, 71, 60) it gets the higher grade, so exactly 92 is an 'A' and 90 is a 'B'; scores are never rounded, so 91.99 or 91.9999999 is a 'B' and 59.99 is an 'F'.
grade_letter: Whenever the score is above 100 or below 0 it returns 'X'. Exactly 0 is valid and returns 'F'. Exactly 100 is valid and returns 'A'.
grade_letter: Whenever the score is NULL, it returns NULL.
grade_letter: Whenever the score is text holding a number ('95', ' 85 ', '89.5', '1e2'), it is read as that number; text that starts with a number ('85%', '90abc') uses the leading number.

grade_letter: Whenever the score is empty or blank text (nothing in it, or only spaces or other whitespace), it is not a number and returns NULL, not 'F'. Whenever the score is text with no leading number ('abc', 'A', '-', '0x5A'), it is also not a number and returns NULL, not 'F'. Whenever the score is the boolean true, it is still treated as 0 and returns 'F' rather than NULL.

late_fee: Whenever an invoice is late by a positive number of days, the first 5 days late are free, so only the days beyond the 5th are charged. An invoice late by 5 days or fewer has no fee. For each charged day the fee is 0.5% of the invoice amount in cents, and the total is rounded down to a whole number of cents. The fee has a minimum of 500 cents, and it is capped at 20% of the invoice amount in cents, rounded down. The cap wins over the minimum, so on a small invoice where 20% of the invoice is less than 500 cents, the fee is that 20% amount. Example: 10000 cents, 10 days late: 5 charged days give 250, raised to the 500 minimum, so the fee is 500. The cap here is 2000.

late_fee: Whenever the fee is not a whole number of cents, it is rounded to the nearest cent with exact halves rounded up. The first 5 days late are always free and are taken off before the fee is worked out, so an invoice late by 5 days or fewer has a fee of 0, whatever its amount (100 cents for 1 day late gives 0; 100 cents for 3 days late gives 0). Examples of the rounding, counting only the days beyond the 5th: 1 cent for 100 days gives 0 (95 charged days give 0.475 cents); 1 cent for 99 days gives 0; 99 cents for 10 days gives 2 (5 charged days give 2.475 cents).
late_fee: Whenever days late is zero or negative (not late), or the invoice amount is zero or negative, the fee is 0.
late_fee: Whenever either the amount or the days late is NULL, it returns NULL.

Whenever days late is a fraction (such as 2.5), it is first rounded down to a whole number of days (2.5 counts as 2, 7.9 counts as 7, 0.9 counts as 0), and only then are the 5 free days taken off and the fee worked out. So 10000 cents for 2.5 days gives 0, because 2 days is within the 5 free days; 10000 cents for 7.5 days counts as 7 days, so 2 charged days give 100, raised to the 500 minimum, so the fee is 500. This applies the same way to a fractional number given as text (for example '2.5' counts as 2 days). A fractional amount (1000.5) is still used as is before the final rounding to a whole cent.

late_fee: Whenever the amount or days late is text, a number in the text is used ('10000' and '10' give 500; '3 days' counts as 3); empty text or text with no leading number counts as 0, so the fee is 0 and not NULL.

Whenever the weight is valid, not over 30000 g, and the zone is valid, the charge is zone x (300 + 100 x the number of started kilograms) cents, where any part of a kilogram counts as a whole one (500 g in zone 1 gives 400; exactly 1000 g gives 400; 1001 g gives 500; 2500 g in zone 2 gives 1200). A weight over 30000 g (30 kg) is not priced this way: it is a flat 9999 whatever the zone, as in rule 37, so a 100 kg pallet to zone 3 costs 9999, not 30900.
shipping_cost: Whenever the weight is exactly 0, the charge is the base amount only: zone x 300 cents (zone 3 gives 900), and the fractional weight 0.5 g counts as one started kilogram.
shipping_cost: Whenever the weight is negative, it returns NULL.

shipping_cost: A zone that is not a number at all (empty text, 'abc', 'A'), is not a whole number (1.5), or is outside 1 to 3 (below 1, meaning zero or negative, or above 3) is billed as zone 3, and it does not return NULL. A whole-valued zone like 2.0 or '1.0' is accepted as that zone number. There is no zone above 3, so zone 100 is billed as zone 3.
shipping_cost: Whenever the weight or zone is NULL, it returns NULL.

shipping_cost: Whenever the weight is text, a number in the text is used ('500', '2kg' counts as 2 g); empty text or text with no leading number counts as a weight of 0 (charged only the base amount), while text with a leading number in the zone ('2z' is zone 2) is accepted.
shipping_cost: Whenever the weight is over 30000 g, the charge is a flat 9999, whatever the zone (for example, 1,000,000,000 g in zone 1 gives 9999). A weight of exactly 30000 g is priced normally.
tiered_price: Whenever the quantity is under 10, the total is the unit price times the quantity with no discount (250 cents x 5 gives 1250).

tiered_price: Whenever the quantity is 10 to 49 units, the whole order, not just the units above 10, gets 10% off (250 x 10 gives 2250; 250 x 11 gives 2475), so 10 units can cost the same as 9 units (2250 each). Whenever the quantity is 50 or more, with no upper limit, the whole order, not just the units above 50, gets 20% off, so 50 or more units always earns a bigger discount than 10 to 49 units (1000 cents x 100 gives 80000, not 90000).

tiered_price: The total is rounded to the nearest 5 cents, with exact halves rounded up, so the total is always a multiple of 5 cents (1 cent x 10 gives 10; 1 cent x 15 gives 15; 1 cent x 25 gives 25; 99.5 cents x 3 gives 300).
tiered_price: Whenever the quantity is 0 or less (zero or any negative quantity), or the unit price is 0, the total is 0, never NULL and never a refund (minus 2 items at 1000 cents gives 0).
tiered_price: Whenever the unit price is negative, it returns NULL, unless the quantity is 0 or less, in which case the total is 0. A negative quantity no longer returns NULL: it gives 0.
tiered_price: Whenever either the unit price or quantity is NULL, it returns NULL.
tiered_price: Whenever the quantity is a fraction, it is used as is and the discount applies only when it is 10 or more (9.99 gives no discount, 250 x 9.99 gives 2498; 10.0 gets the discount).

tiered_price: Whenever the price or quantity is text, a number in the text is used ('250' and '10' give 2250; '12x' counts as 12); empty text or text with no leading number counts as 0, so the total is 0 and not NULL.

weighted_rating: Whenever the rating and the number of votes are valid and there are at least 5 votes, the result is (votes x average rating + 30) / (votes + 10), that is the average pulled toward a neutral prior of 3.0 that is worth 10 votes (5.0 with 10 votes gives 4.0; 4.5 with 100 votes gives 4.36). With fewer than 5 votes this calculation is not used and the result is NULL (see rule 48).
weighted_rating: Whenever the result is calculated, it is rounded to 2 decimal places with exact halves rounded up, and is returned as a decimal number (4.0, not 4).
weighted_rating: Whenever there are fewer than 5 votes, including 0 votes, the result is NULL. Exactly 5 votes is accepted.
weighted_rating: Whenever the votes are negative, it returns NULL; whenever either the rating or the votes are NULL, it returns NULL.

weighted_rating: Whenever the average rating lies outside any normal scale (0, negative or above 5, such as -2 or 7), it is not rejected or limited and is used as given (rating 0 with 10 votes gives 1.5; rating 7 with 10 votes gives 5.0).
weighted_rating: Whenever the votes are a fraction (2.5), they are used as is in the calculation.

weighted_rating: Whenever the rating or votes are text, a number in the text is used ('5' and '10' give 4.0); empty text or text with no leading number counts as 0, so a rating of 'abc' counts as rating 0 (giving 1.5 with 10 votes) and votes of 'abc' counts as 0 votes (giving NULL, because fewer than 5 votes always gives NULL).
gross_receipts: Whenever a group of rows is totalled, it adds up only the amounts that are greater than zero; negative amounts (refunds) are left out and not subtracted (100, -50, 300 gives 400).
gross_receipts: Whenever an amount is NULL or exactly 0, it adds nothing to the total.

gross_receipts: Whenever there are no rows, only NULL amounts, or only zero or negative amounts (including text that counts as 0), there are no valid rows and the total is NULL (blank), not 0. This holds everywhere the total is shown or used, including a single day, period or group with no payments at all, which comes back blank (NULL) and never 0.

gross_receipts: Whenever every counted amount is a whole number, the total is a whole number; whenever any counted amount has decimals the total is a decimal number (100.5 and 200 give 300.5), using ordinary floating point addition (0.1 and 0.2 give 0.30000000000000004).

gross_receipts: Whenever amounts are text, a number in the text is used ('100' and '250.5' give 350.5; '12x' counts as 12; '1e2' counts as 100.0); text with no leading number counts as 0 and adds nothing.

gross_receipts: Whenever it is used with GROUP BY, each group is totalled separately by the same rules (a group with only refunds, or with no valid rows, gives NULL), and rows removed by WHERE are not counted.
gross_receipts: Whenever DISTINCT is written inside it, it is ignored and every row is still added (amounts 5, 5, 3 give 13, not 8).

slugify: Whenever a title is given, it returns the text in lower case with every run of characters that are not letters a-z or digits 0-9 (spaces, punctuation, tabs, line breaks, underscores, symbols) replaced by one single dash ('Hello, World!' gives 'hello-world'; 'snake_case' gives 'snake-case').
slugify: Whenever the result would begin or end with a dash (leading or trailing spaces or punctuation, such as '  Hello   World  ' or '--Hello--'), those dashes are removed.

slugify: Whenever the title has accented letters, they are reduced to the plain letter ('Café Crème Brûlée' gives 'cafe-creme-brulee'; 'Ça va' gives 'ca-va'), and full-width letters and digits, ligatures and superscripts are also converted to plain ones ('ﬁne' gives 'fine', 'x²' gives 'x2').

slugify: Whenever a letter has no plain-letter form (ß, Æ, Ø, and all non-Latin scripts such as Japanese, and emoji), it is silently deleted rather than turned into a dash or transliterated ('Straße' gives 'strae'; 'Ærø Øl ß' gives 'r-l'; '日本語 Tokyo' gives 'tokyo').

slugify: Whenever the title has typographic dashes or quotes (en dash, em dash, curly quotes), they are deleted and not turned into a dash, so the words either side are joined ('a–b—c' gives 'abc'). A plain apostrophe is also deleted, not turned into a dash ('dog's' gives 'dogs').

slugify: Whenever the finished result would be empty, it returns 'untitled' instead, never NULL and never empty text. This covers a title that is empty, spaces only, punctuation only such as '!!!', only non-Latin characters or emoji, only letters that get deleted (such as 'ß'), or any mix of these, because after all the other steps (lower-casing, dash replacement, accent reduction, deleting letters with no plain form, deleting typographic dashes and quotes and plain apostrophes, and trimming leading and trailing dashes) nothing is left. A NULL title still returns NULL.
slugify: Whenever the title is NULL, it returns NULL.
slugify: Whenever the input is a number (12345 or 12.5), it is treated as its text and a decimal point becomes a dash ('12-5').

mask_card: Whenever a card number has 13 to 16 digits (counting digits only, without spaces), it replaces every digit except the last 4 with '*' and shows those last 4 digits, so there is one '*' for every masked digit. Spaces stay exactly where they are ('4111 1111 1111 1111' gives '**** **** **** 1111'; '4111111111111111' gives '************1111'). The number of '*' plus the shown digits equals the number of digits. Whenever the number has more than 16 digits (counting digits only, without spaces or hyphens), it returns 'INVALID' because the number is too long to be a card number, and no digits are shown and no '*' are returned ('4111-1111-1111-1111-123' has 19 digits and gives 'INVALID').

mask_card: Spaces and hyphens in the number stay exactly where they are, and the digits are masked as before, so that only the last four digits are shown and every other digit is replaced with '*' ('4111-1111-1111-1111' gives '****-****-****-1111'). Any other non-digit character, such as dots, slashes, underscores or brackets, makes it return 'INVALID'.

mask_card: Whenever the number has at least 1 digit but fewer than 13 digits (counting digits only, without spaces or hyphens), it returns 'INVALID' because the number is too short to be a card number, and no digits are shown and no '*' are returned ('411' gives 'INVALID'; '1234' gives 'INVALID'; '0000' gives 'INVALID'; '4111 1111 111' gives 'INVALID').

mask_card: Whenever the input has no digits at all and is empty text, it returns empty text. Whenever the input has no digits at all but contains letters or other text (such as 'abcd'), it returns 'INVALID' because letters are not a card number, and no digits are shown and no '*' are returned.
mask_card: Whenever the input is NULL, it returns NULL.

mask_card: Whenever the input has letters or other text mixed with digits, only the digits count, and the last 4 digits found are shown even if they come from other text, provided there are 13 to 16 digits in total (with fewer than 13 digits or more than 16 digits it returns 'INVALID'). Spaces stay where they are, and the letters, any existing '*', and other dropped text are removed ('4111 1111 1111 1111 exp 12/26' has 20 digits in total, so it gives 'INVALID'; 'XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-1111' gives 'INVALID', because the X's and any existing '*' are dropped and only 4 digits remain, which is fewer than 13).

mask_card: Whenever the input is a plain number rather than text (4111111111111111), it is treated as its digits and masked in the same way, including the rule that fewer than 13 digits gives 'INVALID'; a number with a decimal point such as 41.5 counts its digits and not the point (3 digits, so it gives 'INVALID').
mask_card: Whenever digits are written in non-Western numerals (such as Arabic-Indic digits), they are counted as digits and the last four are shown as written.
Nothing else. Enter
